 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

 On The 12th Of November,

 Tejbahadur Singh

 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Other

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Abhishek Rathore - Advocate for the petitio
 Shri Mayank Mishra - G.A./P.L. for respondents/S
 Order
1] Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India against the order dated 26.09.2023, passed by the respondent No.5 Chief Probation and Welfare Officer, Jail Head Office/Director General, Bhopal affirming the order dated 04.01.2023 passed by the respondent No.3 District Magistrate, Neemuch whereby the petitioner's furlough application has been rejected.

entities.text: Chief Probation and Welfare Officer, Jail Head Office/Director General, Bhopal
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: 3] In brief, the facts of the case are that the petitioner stands convicted under Section 377 of IPC and Section 3/ 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and has been sentenced NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:34309 WP No.12877-2024 to imprisonment for life in S.T. No.37 of 2020, vide judgement dated 10.01.2022.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, he is entitled to be released on furlough under Rule 3 of The M.P. Prisoners Leave Rules, 1989 (in short 'the Rules of 1989'), however, the same has been denied by the respondents without any justification.
This is despite good behavior maintained by the petitioner in prison, and a character certificate to this effect has also been issued to him by the Ashtkon Officer, Central Jail, Ujjain.

4] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the other case registered against the petitioner at Crime No.353 of 2017 has already resulted in his acquittal in S.T. No.47 of 2017 vide judgement Tejbahadur Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114030455/
1 dated 15.02.2019.

entities.text: Tejbahadur Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the impugned orders be quashed, and the petitioner may be allowed to be released from the jail.

5] Counsel has also relied upon a decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Atbir Vs.
State of NCT of Delhi reported as 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 427.

entities.text:
Atbir Vs.
State of NCT of Delhi reported as 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 427
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6] Shri Mayank Mishra, learned Counsel for the respondents/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the petitioner has been convicted in a serious offence of abusing a child, and furlough of a prisoner is not a right, but a concession granted to him, and he has no absolute legal right to claim the same, and has also relied upon a decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of State of M.P. & Others Vs. Khuman Singh and another, Cr.A. No.2562 of 2014 dated 10.12.2014 in which it has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:34309 WP No.12877-2024 been opined by the Supreme Court that High Court cannot release the prisoner, and can only direct the competent authority to pass appropriate orders.

entities.text: State of M.P. & Others Vs. Khuman Singh and another, Cr.A. No.2562 of 2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the petition being devoid of merits, is liable to be dismissed.
7] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8] From the record, it is found that the petitioner has been convicted under Section 377 of IPC and Section 3/ 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and has been sentenced to imprisonment for life in S.T.
No.37 of 2020, vide judgement dated 10.01.2022, and apparently his application under Rule 5-A of the Rules of 1989 has been rejected holding that he was involved in serious offence, and if released,
it would give wrong signal to the society, and also that the Surety proposed by the petitioner is not competent to control the petitioner's activity.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This Court is of the considered opinion that if the respondents were of the opinion that the Surety was not competent enough to control the petitioner's activity, then they could have asked him to provide different Surety.
It is also found that he has already been acquitted in another serious offence involving under Section 376 of IPC.
9] In such circumstances, the respondents were required to pass the order strictly, in accordance with the provisions of the Rules of 1989 and M.P. Prisoners Act, 1900.
The respondents have also not stated that under which provision of the aforesaid Act or the Rules, the petitioner has been denied the relief.

In such circumstances, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:34309 WP No.12877-2024 impugned orders dated 04.01.2023 and 26.09.2023 are hereby quashed, and the matter is remanded back to the prison authorities to decide the petitioner's application afresh, in accordance with law, preferably, within three weeks' time
10] With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Tejbahadur Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114030455/
